name: Hoshimono
tagline: A concept online supermarket with same-day delivery slots.
summary: Groceries from browsing to the doorstep: a searchable catalogue, a cart, delivery slots, cash on delivery or online payment, and the staff screens that pick, pack and send every order from one hub.

cover.caption: The storefront: aisles, fresh picks and the delivery promise up top.

gallery.alt: Chicken Adobo recipe with its ingredients list
gallery.caption: Recipe to cart: ingredients scale with the servings, and pantry staples start unticked.
Search understands Filipino and typos: "gatas" finds six kinds of milk.

gallery.alt: Carabao Mangoes product page, sold by weight
gallery.caption: A Product sold by weight, with a plain note on how the final price is set.
The cart, with a substitute choice and picker notes for every item.
Checkout holds the chosen two-hour slot while the shopper pays.
Staff see what is on the shelf, reserved and free, with low stock flagged.
The storefront in dark mode, which follows the system setting.

gallery.alt: A product page on a phone
gallery.caption: A Product page on a phone.

features: Browse aisles or search in English or Filipino, typos included.
Fill a cart, choose a substitute for each item, and leave notes for the picker.
Pick a two-hour delivery slot, then pay by GCash, card or cash on delivery.
Recipes that add their ingredients to the cart, scaled to the servings.
Staff screens for orders, picking, dispatch, cash, stock, slots and refunds.
The whole shop in Filipino, and an installable app with offline basics.

build.title: Weighed items, settled fairly
build.body: Items sold by weight charge an estimate at checkout, settle to the packed weight at picking (never above the estimate) and refund the difference in one go.

build.title: The last unit sells once
build.body: Tests race orders for the last unit and carts for one slot against a real Postgres database.

build.title: Payments behind one interface
build.body: PayMongo and a stand-in provider share one interface, and every webhook is deduplicated before it touches an Order.

build.title: A modular monolith
build.body: 13 modules talk only through their index files, enforced by an ESLint rule that has its own test.

build.title: Search on plain Postgres
build.body: Full-text search, trigrams and a Filipino and English synonym list, with no search service to run.

build.title: Checked on every merge
build.body: 391 Vitest tests, 81 Playwright tests with axe accessibility checks, and Lighthouse budgets. 22 decision records explain the choices.

nodes.name: Shoppers
nodes.detail: Find groceries, fill a cart, choose a delivery time and pay, in English or Filipino.

nodes.name: Staff
nodes.detail: Pick and pack the orders, send them out, and keep the stock and refunds in order.

nodes.name: The Hoshimono shop
nodes.detail: One website for shoppers and staff, made of 13 parts that each look after one job: the catalogue, the cart, prices, orders, payments, stock, delivery and more.

nodes.name: Database
nodes.detail: Keeps the products, stock, orders and delivery times, and powers the search.

nodes.name: Online payments
nodes.detail: Takes payments and gives refunds. Each payment message is checked, so the same payment is never counted twice.

nodes.name: Emails and text messages
nodes.detail: Ready to plug in: for now the messages are only written to a log, until real accounts are set up.
